messages:
alertbot: 🚨 alert — 5xx rate on /v1/generate jumped to 38% (5m) in us-east-1, Canary pool `canary-042` showing spike. Metric: http_502_count.
marie_oncall: I'm looking. Is this the canary rollout from this morning? @raj_engineer did the routing flag go out?
raj_engineer: yes we flipped `route.scope=canary-042` at 09:12 during the staged rollout. I validated the canary traffic target but not the full route table. Doing quick check now.
jia_sre: seeing timeouts and 502s with fast fail at the envoy layer, logs show upstream health check flapping for model-serving-pool-canary.
sam_support: multiple customers reporting generate API 502s and some billing spikes due to retries. Customer incident pages open. I'm triaging priority customers now.
raj_engineer: pulling deploy manifest — suspect flag serialization: in the orchestration manifest the key was `route.scope: canary-042/` (note trailing slash). The route selector library treats that as a prefix and matched `*` earlier than intended. Possible scope bleed to stable routes.
luis_product: ugh, that would explain why canary is getting much more traffic than planned. We need immediate rollback or containment.
marie_oncall: options: 1) revert flag (deploy rollback) 2) apply emergency override to kube-service routing 3) scale canary down to 0. Which is fastest?
jia_sre: fastest is to scale the canary pool down to 0 replicas and then revert the manifest. I can scale it down via k8s patch now.
raj_engineer: prepping rollback artifact now. I pushed a rollback candidate tag `canary-rollback-1766` to the images registry.
marie_oncall: @jia_sre please scale down, @deploy-bot coordinate the rollback once scaled. Sam, keep customers updated, add note about retries/backoff.
deploy-bot: running `kubectl -n inference scale deploy canary-042 --replicas=0` (user: jia_sre).
(deploy-bot): `Scaling deployment "canary-042" to 0 replicas`
jia_sre: scaled to 0. Observability: 502s dropping — now at 7% across the fleet, still above baseline but trending down.
raj_engineer: applying manifest revert: removing trailing slash from `route.scope` key and re-applying config. Command: ```
kubectl apply -f s3://configs/orch/2026-03-15/route-manifest.yaml --record
# manifest change: route.scope: canary-042 -> route.scope: canary-042
```
luis_product: confirm we didn't accidentally remove any canary-only policies (timeouts/connection pools) while reverting.
raj_engineer: double-checked — only the key normalization fixed. No policy changes.
sam_support: FYI customers who reported high error rates: CX-1252, CX-1301, CX-1307. Notified them of active rollback and ETA ~15m.
marie_oncall: telemetry now: 5xx at 2.1% in the past 3m. Latency back to normal for stable routes. Good.
jia_sre: adding a temporary WAF rule to drop header `X-Route-Override` to avoid weird client-supplied routing. Also increasing envoy circuit-breaker thresholds while we stabilize.
raj_engineer: root cause hypothesis: route selector library treated trailing slash as wildcard prefix; config validation should have rejected trailing slashes. Filing a config lint rule now.
luis_product: schedule postmortem and communicate to releases team — need to add stricter canary isolation checks in rollout playbook.
sam_support: opening follow-up support tickets for impacted customers with credits and explanation.
marie_oncall: current action items: (1) ensure canary replicas remain 0 until safe (2) coordinate rollback PR to enforce strict route-key schema (3) update runbook with quick mitigation commands. Assign owners: raj -> PR, jia -> canary scaling confirmation & envoy tweaks, sam -> customer comms.
raj_engineer: PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/orchestration/pulls/492 with schema validation.
marie_oncall: 5xx rates back to baseline (<0.5%) for the last 5m. Closing incident in 10m if stable. Any objections?
luis_product: no objections. Good job everyone.
sam_support: will follow up with targeted emails and support credits.
raj_engineer: follow-up note — will add unit test in route-selector for trailing slash case.
jia_sre: monitoring alerts adjusted to suppress noisy alerts during rollback — will restore after postmortem.
marie_oncall: incident resolved, creating postmortem ticket and linking logs + timeline. Thank you. :tada:
